Validate a Multivariate Distribution

Source: R/check_distrib_mv.R
check_distrib_mv.Rd

Runs the battery of check_distrib() on a multivariate distribution, where the one-dimensional checks have no counterpart.

Usage

check_distrib_mv(distrib, theta, n, nsim, tol)

Arguments

distrib

A multivariate_distrib() object.

theta

A named list of parameters, already aligned.

n

The number of observations drawn for the derivative checks.

nsim

The Monte Carlo sample size.

tol

The tolerance of the gradient and response-derivative comparisons, applied to the absolute difference divided by the larger of one and the magnitude of the reference; the Hessian comparison uses 10 * tol. The other checks use fixed thresholds.

Value

A list of one-row data frames, as check_distrib() builds.

Details

Five of the univariate checks have no counterpart in \(p\) dimensions: the integration of the density by one-dimensional quadrature, the two checks of the distribution function (its range and its agreement with the density), the quantile round trip, and the comparison of the generator with the distribution function. The distribution function is an integral over an orthant, and the quantile function inverts an ordering that does not exist in several dimensions. Reporting these checks as failures would mark a correct family as defective, and a user validating their own distribution could not tell a real defect from them.

The battery runs the checks that do generalize:

  1. the density is positive and finite on a sample;

  2. the density integrates to one. For a family that enumerates its support through mv_support() this is an exact sum over that support, with tolerance 1e-10; otherwise it is importance sampling from the proposal that mv_reference_draw() supplies, with tolerance 20 / sqrt(nsim). The default proposal is a gaussian with the same mean and twice the covariance; the Student \(t\) uses a Student \(t\) with half the degrees of freedom and twice the scale matrix, and the Dirichlet the uniform law on the simplex. The proposal is not the distribution itself, which would make the ratio identically one;

  3. the score has mean zero, the first Bartlett identity, under the distribution's own generator, so it is also a check that the generator and the density describe the same law;

  4. gradient and Hessian against finite differences of the summed log-density;

  5. the expected information against the Monte Carlo average of the observed Hessian, and against the variance of the score, which is the second Bartlett identity;

  6. the generator against the first two moments. When the mean or the covariance of the family is not finite (a Student \(t\) with \(\nu \le 2\)) the row has no statistic, and check_distrib() lists it among the skipped checks with that reason. The tolerance is 20 / sqrt(nsim), which assumes a finite fourth moment: for a Student \(t\) with \(2 < \nu \le 4\) the sample covariance has no variance, and the row can fail with a correct generator;

  7. the response derivatives against finite differences in \(y\).

The last of these is run only when it applies, as the univariate battery omits the checks that have no counterpart for a discrete family. A family with an enumerable support is discrete and has no derivative in the response, and the multivariate base class signals an error for distrib_grad_y(), so a family that has not registered a method has no response derivatives by design, and the check is omitted for it.
